behavioral_effects: None stated. An empty list is a claim that nothing observably changes.
compatibility_impact: The file download response contract gains X-Content-Type-Options and a stronger CSP on active types; Content-Disposition behavior is unchanged and covered by a test. HTML/SVG previews in the chat file-preview iframe now render sandboxed: markup displays, scripts and same-origin requests inside previews no longer run. PDF, image, text previews unchanged.
reason: Security finding: text/html is an allowed upload type and /api/files/[id] serves it inline while replacing the CSP with only frame-ancestors, so uploaded HTML runs JavaScript same-origin - the enabling step for refresh-token theft
rollback: git revert restores the permissive headers; doing so reopens the same-origin execution finding.
security_impact: Closes the same-origin HTML execution finding: active content types (text/html, xhtml, xml, svg) are now served with CSP 'sandbox; frame-ancestors self', which renders them in a unique opaque origin with scripts disabled, on both the FastAPI route and the Next.js proxy handler (which previously replaced the backend CSP with only frame-ancestors). X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff added on both hops; the proxy fails closed to a sandbox CSP if the backend header is ever missing. This removes the demonstrated path to same-origin bearer-token theft via /api/auth/refresh. text/html remains an allowed upload type by design (preview and agent-reading use cases); it is inert when served.
summary: Stop uploaded HTML from executing scripts on the application origin
